title: Pointed regular strict local ind-etale limit of a divisor
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], let $g\in R$ be a nonzerodivisor with regular quotient $R/(g)$, and let $y\in\operatorname{Spec}R$ contain $g$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. There are a commutative ring $H$ in the same universe and a ring homomorphism $\iota:R\to H$ which is ind-etale (a filtered colimit of etale $R$-algebras). The ring $H$ is strictly henselian local (henselian with separably closed residue field), $H$ and $H/(\iota(g))$ are regular local, $\iota(g)$ is a nonzerodivisor in the maximal ideal of $H$, and some point $x\in\operatorname{Spec}H$ maps to $y$.

source.place: Tag 0EYG, strict henselization paragraph; Tags 04GP, 04HX, 06LN and 05WS

proof.text: Take Ω to be the algebraic closure of κ(y), and barY to be its canonical geometric point of Spec R. Let H be the existing canonical pointed-neighbourhood colimit strictHenselizationRing barY. Apply strictHenselizationResidue, the residue clause of lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality, to obtain strict henselianity and the closed-point image. Take b to be the ring map recovered by full faithfulness of Spec from the canonical structural morphism. Spec.map b equals that morphism.

Apply smallStrictHenselization_indEtale_of_affine_chart to the identity affine chart and identity presentation of Spec H. This proves b is ind-etale over R. The closed-point image is y; taking the asIdeal of this equality identifies contraction of the maximal ideal with y. Thus b(g) belongs to the maximal ideal, hence is not a unit.

Apply strictHenselization_regular_divisor_quotient to g. It supplies regularity and a domain structure for H/(b(g)). A nonzero quotient of a local ring is local, so Mathlib IsLocalRing.of_surjective' and IsRegularLocalRing.of_isRegularRing_of_isLocalRing make this quotient regular local.

Apply that same comparison to 0: its hypotheses do not require a nonzerodivisor. Transport regularity of R to R/(0) using RingEquiv.quotientBot and Ideal.quotEquivOfEq. The image of zero is not a unit because H is nonzero. The comparison yields regularity of H/(0), which transports back to H. Since H is local, IsRegularLocalRing.of_isRegularRing_of_isLocalRing gives ambient regular locality.

Give H the algebra structure induced by b. Ind-etaleness implies weak etaleness, hence flatness, by the upstream proved instance Algebra.IndEtale.weaklyEtale. Mathlib IsSMulRegular.of_flat transports the supplied injective multiplication by g. Assemble the preceding properties with the closed point of H. These are direct applications of existing instances and the flat base-change lemma.

lean.statement:
theorem regular_divisor_strict_local_limit
    (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (g : R) [IsRegularRing R]
    (hg : IsSMulRegular R g) [IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {g})]
    (y : Spec R) (hy : g ∈ y.asIdeal) :
    ∃ (H : CommRingCat.{u}) (ι : R →+* H),
      ι.IndEtale ∧
      ∃ (hH : IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing H),
        IsRegularLocalRing H ∧ IsRegularLocalRing (H ⧸ Ideal.span {ι g}) ∧
        IsSMulRegular H (ι g) ∧
        ι g ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal H ∧
        ∃ x : Spec H, (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ι)) x = y
